description: The configuration registry itself (D-068): where its change store lives, how it refuses secrets and what its literal check scans.

config.guard_key_words.description: snake_case words (or word sequences) that make a parameter key name a secret; such a key must hold only the secret's name. A bare 'token' is not one (a lexer token, a token budget); a token-shaped value is refused by config.guard_value_patterns and the entropy test whatever its key.

config.guard_name_suffixes.description: Key endings that mark a parameter holding a secret's environment variable name, never its value.

config.guard_name_pattern.description: The shape of a secret's name (an environment variable name) that a secret-name key may hold.

config.guard_value_patterns.description: Shapes of a secret value (vendor token prefixes, private keys, signed tokens, credentials in a URL); a registry value or a set value that matches is refused.

config.guard_entropy_min_length.description: Shortest unbroken token-alphabet string the entropy test judges as a possible random secret.

config.guard_entropy_min_bits.description: Shannon entropy per character from which such a string is refused as a random secret; a hex digest (at most 4 bits) is not.

config.guard_entropy_alphabet.description: The alphabet of a random secret (base64 and URL-safe base64) the entropy test applies to.

config.store_adapter.description: Which forge_events adapter holds the config.changed log: file keeps it in the checkout (config.store_dir), the only store since D-300: the shared value of a key is its registry file in git, changed by a PR, and a change through the store is a machine-local override. The control store (the control plane's event log and its versioned key, VAZÃO F35) left the enum (D-300, SEMENTE §6: no double path). Read from this file, never from the store itself.
config.store_adapter.x-source: TR1; D-068 (3); D-065 (2); ORIGIN-FINISH (CONFIG-STORE-CONTROL); D-300 (VAZÃO F61): internal questions leave Cloudflare, the file store by default

config.store_dir.description: Directory of the file adapter's log, relative to the checkout (gitignored). Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.store_cache_ttl_s.description: How long one read of a remote change store (an adapter whose log lives off this machine, e.g. github) serves config.get in this checkout before the log is read again: the most a value set by another session can lag here. A change through this checkout's store refreshes it at once. Read from this file, never from the store itself. Five minutes since 03/11 (VAZÃO F28, I-5102f4e9): with one cache per checkout and many worktrees, a minute made the control plane's 5,000,000 rows read a day run out.

config.store_cache_dir.description: Directory, relative to the checkout (gitignored), of the snapshot file that lets every process of this checkout share one read of a remote change store per config.store_cache_ttl_s. Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.store_quarantine_log.description: File, relative to the checkout (gitignored, append-only JSON Lines), where the change store's reader records each envelope of the log the port refuses (event_id, type, reason). The log is append-only, so such an event is skipped, never fatal; it is said on stderr the first time this checkout sees it. Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.store_stale_max_s.description: How long after a remote read of the change store expires (config.store_cache_ttl_s) it may still serve config.get in this checkout while the store cannot be read (the forge refuses, rate-limits or does not answer); each serve is said once per process on stderr. Past it the read error stands. One hour covers GitHub's longest limit window. 0 turns the fallback off. Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.bootstrap_owners.description: Registry owners whose parameters configure the machine bootstrap (scripts/cloud/setup.sh, env.sh, toolchain.py, postgres.py; env-premises: session_identity.py) before any session state exists: config.get returns their registry value and never reads the shared change store, so a session starts while the forge refuses or rate-limits reads; scripts/config refuses to change them (edit the registry file). Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.literal_check_roots.description: The engine and tooling paths the structure check scans for literals of registered parameters.

config.literal_check_excludes.description: Path prefixes inside those roots that are not scanned for literals: generated types only (the generated drift stage checks them). Tests are scanned like any engine file (LT1).

config.literal_check_suffixes.description: File suffixes the literal scan reads (Python, shell, JavaScript modules).

config.literal_check_shebangs.description: Interpreters whose extensionless scripts (by their #! line) the literal scan reads.

config.literal_cache_dir.description: Where the tree checks keep what they extract from one file's text alone (source_facts: the literal scan's Python candidates, unit_map's dynamic selections, literal_census's raw values, vendor_check's strings, argv heads and imports) through the storage port (providers.storage_adapter), keyed by the file's content, the interpreter and the extractor's own source, so every checkout of this user shares them and a registry change never reuses a verdict. A leading ~ is the home directory; CONFIG_LITERAL_CACHE_DIR overrides it for one run; empty turns the cache off.

config.store_window_max.description: The deepest window, in records of the repository channel, a reader of a remote config store reads back to find the newest config.snapshot when the default window (forge-events.git_ref_window) holds none: the window counts records of every kind, so other events (plan notes) can push the snapshot out. It grows by four each step; the channel is never read whole (D-085). Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.store_snapshot_after_events.description: How many config.changed events may follow the newest config.snapshot before a change through this checkout appends a new one. A reader of a remote store reads back only to its newest snapshot, so the log can outgrow forge-events.github_max_pages. Read from this file, never from the store itself.

config.monotonic_patterns.description: Globs of registry parameter names that are thresholds (timeouts, limits, maxima, budgets, ceilings, tolerances). The threshold check of structure-check refuses a numeric default of a matching parameter that loosens against the base without a cited decision; a match is a ceiling unless the entry declares x-monotonic. The list only grows (D-069 item 14).
config.monotonic_patterns.x-source: TH1; D-069 item 14; enforcement audit 2026-10-26 rule 5
